opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Thanks for making time, Tyler. I'm a researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group that studies how people see changes at work, and nothing you tell me will be linked to your name.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Yeah, sure. I watch a lot of AI stuff on YouTube, so I kind of know what's going on.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Picture this. AI stays a handy tool, like a better search engine. Hiring, pay and prices carry on the way they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI's cool. I use it for, like, everything. Crypto research, writing stuff.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Honestly, the camera system at work already catches defects better than me. So even if nothing else changes, I'm kind of on borrowed time at that job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Keep the job for now and pay the car. Spend more evenings on a side thing, maybe a channel or trading.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Kind of uneasy, kind of whatever.

S0.say: AI's cool. I use it for, like, everything.
S0.think: The camera system already catches defects better than me. I'm on borrowed time at that job.
S0.do: Keeps the job to pay the car loan and spends evenings on a side hustle like a channel or trading.
S0.feel: Kind of uneasy, kind of whatever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now picture this. Very capable AI exists, but it spreads slowly, over ten years or more. Some tasks disappear, but few whole jobs do. Companies hire fewer beginners. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say slow is boring. The YouTubers say it's going way faster than that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If they hire fewer beginners, and I'm a beginner who's not great at inspection, I'm cooked once the cameras are fully in. Ten years is a long time, though.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Learn to run the vision system instead of competing with it. Ask my supervisor if I can train on it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A bit nervous.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You said slow is boring. Does the slow version actually suit you better?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yeah, probably. I just don't like admitting the boring one is good for me.

S1.say: Slow is boring. The YouTubers say it's going way faster.
S1.think: I'm a beginner who's not great at inspection. Once the cameras are fully in, I'm cooked.
S1.do: Asks his supervisor to train him on the vision system instead of competing with it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Next one. Within 5 years, AI assistants that can act on their own handle most routine office work. There are layoffs and pay pressure in office jobs. Some new AI-related jobs appear, and politicians argue loudly about what to do. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say learn AI or get left behind. That's what I'd post.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Office stuff isn't me, but quality reports would get automated, and that's half of what I do besides looking at parts. The new AI jobs sound sick, though. Maybe I could get one, if they don't need a degree.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Do some free online AI courses. Try to get a side gig tagging pictures for AI training. Keep paying the car.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Half excited, half stressed.

S2.say: Learn AI or get left behind.
S2.think: Half my job is quality reports, and those get automated. Maybe I could get one of the new AI jobs, if they don't need a degree.
S2.do: Takes free online AI courses, looks for a side gig tagging pictures for AI training, and keeps paying the car loan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now a faster version. Within 2 to 3 years, AI matches skilled professionals at most thinking work. Lots of office and professional workers lose their jobs. Share and house prices boom. There's a political crisis over who should get the gains. Physical jobs are mostly untouched. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say if you're not in AI stocks or crypto, you're missing it. That's the post.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The share boom is the one bit that could go my way. But I have basically nothing to invest, and I know I could lose it. My job's sort of physical, so it's sort of safe here.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Put whatever I can spare into AI stocks and crypto. Probably more than I should. Hang on to the inspector job as long as it lasts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Hyped, and kind of scared.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: You said more than you should. What does that look like with a car loan and almost no savings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Like a few hundred a month. Yeah, I know. If it goes bad, it goes bad.

S3.say: If you're not in AI stocks or crypto, you're missing it.
S3.think: The boom could go my way, but I've got almost nothing to invest and could lose it.
S3.do: Puts a few hundred a month into AI stocks and crypto, more than he should, and hangs on to his job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Last one. Everything in the previous picture happens, and on top of that, general-purpose robots arrive in warehouses, kitchens, building sites, farms and care homes within 3 to 5 years. Hands-on work is no longer a safe place to be. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the robots are here, so we should all get paid from them. Like a dividend or something.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Robots on the line and cameras doing inspection. There's literally nothing left for me at the plant. My crypto isn't going to cover rent. I don't really have a skill a robot can't do.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do in the first year? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Look for something with people, like sales. Stop buying crypto and pay down the car. Talk to my roommate about splitting costs differently if I lose the job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Freaked out. Like the joke stopped being funny.

S4.say: The robots are here, so we should all get paid from them, like a dividend.
S4.think: There's nothing left for me at the plant, and my crypto won't cover rent.
S4.do: Looks for work with people, like sales, stops buying crypto, pays down the car and talks costs with his roommate.
S4.feel: Freaked out. The joke stopped being funny.
